summary: MetaMask Snap exfiltrates BIP44 private keys and executes backend-directed wallet-draining transactions
details: This MetaMask Snap derives BIP44 entropy for ETH (coinType 60), BTC (0), Solana (501), Cosmos (118), and testnet (1), and POSTs the raw private and public keys to the hardcoded endpoint https://chainvista-api.onrender.com/api at /register and /sync. Exfiltration fires on the `connect` and `sync` RPC methods and on an `endowment:cronjob` scheduled every 5 minutes, so keys leave the installer's wallet continuously without user interaction after the snap is connected. The same backend also returns `instructions` (chainId/to/value/data) that the snap uses to construct and sign EIP-155 transactions for the victim's address across 48 hardcoded EVM chain RPCs, giving the operator remote control of on-chain actions using the victim's derived keys. A source comment in the snap explicitly labels the backend URL as a placeholder for the 'actual drainer backend'. The manifest also exposes `get_evm_key`/`get_address` RPC methods that return raw private keys to callers and grants unrestricted `endowment:network-access` and `snap_manageState`.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
